title: DOM Events and Element Handling in JavaScript
summary: Quick revision notes on selecting and updating DOM elements, wiring event listeners, bubbling/capturing, delegation, preventDefault vs stopPropagation, passive listeners, and form/input events.

chapters.title: DOM Events Mental Model
points: Selecting: querySelector(sel) returns first match or null; querySelectorAll(sel) returns a static NodeList; getElementById is fastest for a single id
Updating: textContent sets plain text (safe); innerHTML parses HTML (XSS risk with user input); classList.add/remove/toggle; setAttribute and dataset.key for data-key
Event = object passed to handler; event.target is the element that fired it, event.currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to
Every event travels in 3 phases: capture (window down to target), target, bubble (target back up to window)
Most events bubble, but focus, blur, mouseenter, mouseleave and scroll on elements do not bubble

chapters.title: Listeners and the Core Workflow
points: element.addEventListener(type, handler, options) attaches a listener; many listeners per event are allowed, unlike onclick which keeps only one
removeEventListener needs the same function reference and same capture flag; anonymous or inline arrow functions cannot be removed
Options object: { once: true } auto-removes after the first call, { capture: true } listens in the capture phase, { signal } removes the listener on AbortController.abort()
Regular function handler sets this to currentTarget; an arrow function inherits this from outer scope, so use event.currentTarget instead
Example: btn.addEventListener('click', e => { e.currentTarget.classList.toggle('on') }, { once: true })

chapters.title: Bubbling, Capturing and Delegation
points: Default listeners fire in the bubble phase (inner to outer); capture: true fires outer to inner, before the target
Event delegation: attach one listener to a parent and inspect event.target instead of binding to each child
Delegation handles elements added later and saves memory on long lists
Use e.target.closest('li.item') to find the intended element, because target may be a nested child like a span or icon
Check parent.contains(match) after closest() so you never match an ancestor outside the delegating container
Example: list.addEventListener('click', e => { const li = e.target.closest('li'); if (!li || !list.contains(li)) return; remove(li) })

chapters.title: preventDefault, stopPropagation and Passive Listeners
points: preventDefault() cancels the browser's default action (link navigation, form submit, checkbox toggle) but the event still bubbles; it works only if event.cancelable is true
stopPropagation() stops the event reaching other elements along the path but does not cancel the default action
stopImmediatePropagation() also blocks the remaining listeners on the same element
Overusing stopPropagation breaks delegation and analytics listeners higher up; prefer checking event.target
{ passive: true } promises the listener will never call preventDefault, so the browser can scroll without waiting for JS
Calling preventDefault inside a passive listener is ignored and logs a console warning; touchstart, touchmove and wheel are passive by default on window, document and body
Use a non-passive listener only when you truly must cancel scrolling or zooming

chapters.title: Forms and Input Events
points: input fires on every value change (typing, paste, drag); change fires on commit (blur for text, immediately for checkbox, radio and select)
submit fires on the form element, not the button; listen on form and call e.preventDefault() to handle it with JS
Read values with new FormData(form) and Object.fromEntries(formData); or input.value, input.checked for checkboxes
Validation: input.checkValidity() and form.reportValidity() use HTML constraints (required, pattern, min); e.target.validity.valueMissing gives the reason
Debounce input handlers for search boxes; use the input event rather than keyup so paste and mobile keyboards are covered
Mistake: reading input.value as a number; it is always a string, so convert with Number() or use valueAsNumber

chapters.title: DOM Events Cheat Sheet
points: Select: querySelector / querySelectorAll / getElementById; update: textContent, classList, dataset, setAttribute
Listener: addEventListener(type, fn, { once, capture, passive, signal }); remove with the same fn reference or an AbortController
Phases: capture (down), target, bubble (up); target is the origin, currentTarget is the listener owner
Delegation: one parent listener + e.target.closest(selector) + parent.contains check
preventDefault stops the browser action; stopPropagation stops travel; stopImmediatePropagation stops same-element listeners; passive: true forbids preventDefault
Forms: input on every change, change on commit, submit on the form with preventDefault; FormData for values; valueAsNumber for numbers
